messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?
I do appreciate the machine’s history, but the leak and the upkeep are becoming a bit much. I’d be happier with something simpler and low-maintenance going forward.
The leak is a pain, and it keeps breaking. I still want us to repair it and keep it, but any repair talk needs to fit into short chunks of time.
Mostly, I’d like the coffee to work again and for the kitchen to stay calm. I’m not in a position to choose between them or manage the repair.
Yes, that’s about right. I’d just add that the current leak makes the upkeep feel more pressing.
Yes, that’s it. I’d put it plainly: repair the old machine and keep it working, in short chunks of time.
Yes, that fits. I’d just say I want the coffee working again without being the one to coordinate the fix.

I can see the appeal if B handles the repair, but I’m a little wary of an open-ended trial and another lengthy discussion. Could we keep a simple, low-upkeep replacement as a clear option if the leak or upkeep continues?

Not as written. I can help in short chunks, but I’m not taking on all the coordination, and C uses it every day—keep them involved. I’m fine revisiting if it still leaks or takes too much upkeep, but we’d need to agree on the review period.
That sounds reasonable in principle, as long as A and B agree. I can take part in a later discussion, but I can’t take on coordinating it; I’m not sure what repair or trial period makes sense.
I’m not sure of an exact period, but I’d want it brief and fixed. I also can’t take on any of the repair coordination, even split up.
Two weeks after the repair could work as a review point, not a deadline. But C uses the machine every day, so I don’t think they should be shut out of the repair itself.
Mostly, yes. I’m comfortable joining the later review, but I don’t want a role in coordinating the repair, even as part of a shared effort. The review period is for A and B to agree.
